_comment: Conventions and budgets per kind of sprite. A game's manifest may override any value or add profiles under "profiles", and one sprite may override values under its own "overrides". Sizes are pixels unless they say units (one unit is one grid cell; a hero is about 1.5 tall). "clips" is where a game states what it expects of each clip: {"walk": {"loop": true, "events": ["step", "step"]}} and so on (see README.md, 'The spec of a sprite'); "clip_kinds" are this kit's conventions for clips of well-known names and "clip_defaults" what holds for every clip. null turns a check off.

default._comment: Anything else. Only what is wrong for every sprite is checked: use a real profile.

character._comment: A figure that stands on the ground and turns: heroes, enemies, townsfolk. Pixel art drawn as a cutout (alpha 0 or 255), four or eight directions, the pivot between the feet, one palette. 'stance' says what a clip's pose is held to: upright (feet on the idle clip's ground row, steady, the same amount of figure as idle, west like east), low (kneeling, lying: on the ground row and steady, but any shape) or air (thrown, jumping: not held to the ground). A clip with no stance is not held to anything: say what each of the game's clips is in the manifest.

prop._comment: A thing drawn as pixel art that does not walk: a chest, a sign, a crystal, a dropped sword. A cutout like a character, but nothing is assumed about its pivot, its size or its clips.

effect._comment: A flipbook played once (or looped) where something happens: a slash, an impact, a spell. Soft alpha, usually drawn additively, so there is no palette or speck check; what matters is that it stays inside its frames, ends, and is not longer than the moment it marks.

image._comment: One still picture drawn through a sprite: a blob shadow, a magic circle, a glow, a ring, a light shaft. The game scales, tints and fades it; the sheet only has to hold it whole.

particle._comment: The sprite of an emitter's particles: the engine plays its 'idle' clip (direction row 0) over each particle's age in seconds, so a clip that does not loop and holds its last frame for longer than any particle lives is the normal form. Particles are tiny and fill their cells; they have no outline and no pivot to speak of.
